title: Mirror Box
statementMd:
Mirror Box is a name of a popular game in the Iranian National Amusement Park (INAP). There is a wooden box, $10^{5}$ cm long and $100$ cm high in this game. Some parts of the box's ceiling and floor are covered by mirrors. There are two negligibly small holes in the opposite sides of the box at heights $*h*_{*l*}$ and $*h*_{*r*}$ centimeters above the floor. The picture below shows what the box looks like.

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/67f143771f3897c417d67602087e9fe625672680.png)

In the game, you will be given a laser gun to shoot once. The laser beam must enter from one hole and exit from the other one. Each mirror has a preset number $*v*_{*i*}$, which shows the number of points players gain if their laser beam hits that mirror. Also — to make things even funnier — the beam must **not** hit any mirror more than once.

Given the information about the box, your task is to find the maximum score a player may gain. Please note that the reflection obeys the law "the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection".

## Input

The first line of the input contains three space-separated integers $*h*_{*l*}, *h*_{*r*}, *n*$ ($0 < *h*_{*l*}, *h*_{*r*} < 100$, $0 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$) — the heights of the holes and the number of the mirrors.

Next $*n*$ lines contain the descriptions of the mirrors. The $*i*$-th line contains space-separated $*v*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*}, *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}$; the integer $*v*_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *v*_{*i*} ≤ 1000$) is the score for the $*i*$-th mirror; the character $*c*_{*i*}$ denotes $*i*$-th mirror's position — the mirror is on the ceiling if $*c*_{*i*}$ equals "`T`" and on the floor if $*c*_{*i*}$ equals "`F`"; integers $*a*_{*i*}$ and $*b*_{*i*}$ ($0 ≤ *a*_{*i*} < *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{5}$) represent the $*x*$-coordinates of the beginning and the end of the mirror.

No two mirrors will share a common point. Consider that the $*x*$ coordinate increases in the direction from left to right, so the border with the hole at height $*h*_{*l*}$ has the $*x*$ coordinate equal to 0 and the border with the hole at height $*h*_{*r*}$ has the $*x*$ coordinate equal to $10^{5}$.

## Output

The only line of output should contain a single integer — the maximum possible score a player could gain.

## Note

The second sample is depicted above. The red beam gets $10 + 50 + 5 + 35 + 8 + 2 = 110$ points and the blue one gets $120$.

**The red beam on the picture given in the statement shows how the laser beam can go approximately, this is just illustration how the laser beam can gain score. So for the second sample there is no such beam that gain score 110.**
statementZhMd:
<statement>
镜箱（Mirror Box）是伊朗国家游乐园（INAP）中一种广受欢迎的游戏名称。游戏中有一个长 $10^{5}$ cm、高 $100$ cm 的木箱。箱子的顶部和底部有些部分覆盖着镜子。在木箱相对的两侧各有一个极小的孔，孔的高度分别为距地面 $*h*_{*l*}$ 厘米和 $*h*_{*r*}$ 厘米。下图展示了木箱的样子。

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/67f143771f3897c417d67602087e9fe625672680.png)

游戏中，你会得到一把激光枪，并可以射击一次。激光束必须从一个孔进入，并从另一个孔射出。每面镜子都有一个预设数值 $*v*_{*i*}$，表示激光束击中该镜子时玩家获得的分数。另外——为了让游戏更加有趣——激光束不能击中同一面镜子超过一次。

给定木箱的信息，请你求出玩家可能获得的最高分数。请注意，反射遵循“入射角等于反射角”的规律。

## 输入格式

输入的第一行包含三个用空格分隔的整数 $*h*_{*l*}, *h*_{*r*}, *n*$（$0 < *h*_{*l*}, *h*_{*r*} < 100$，$0 ≤ *n* ≤ 100$），分别表示孔的高度和镜子的数量。

接下来 $*n*$ 行描述镜子。第 $*i*$ 行包含用空格分隔的 $*v*_{*i*}, *c*_{*i*}, *a*_{*i*}, *b*_{*i*}$；整数 $*v*_{*i*}$（$1 ≤ *v*_{*i*} ≤ 1000$）表示第 $*i*$ 面镜子的分数；字符 $*c*_{*i*}$ 表示第 $*i*$ 面镜子的位置——如果 $*c*_{*i*}$ 等于 "`T`"，则镜子位于顶部；如果 $*c*_{*i*}$ 等于 "`F`"，则镜子位于底部；整数 $*a*_{*i*}$ 和 $*b*_{*i*}$（$0 ≤ *a*_{*i*} < *b*_{*i*} ≤ 10^{5}$）表示镜子起点和终点的 $*x*$ 坐标。

任意两面镜子都不会共享公共点。规定 $*x*$ 坐标从左向右递增，因此，带有高度为 $*h*_{*l*}$ 的孔的边界的 $*x*$ 坐标为 0，带有高度为 $*h*_{*r*}$ 的孔的边界的 $*x*$ 坐标为 $10^{5}$。

## 输出格式

输出的唯一一行应包含一个整数，即玩家可能获得的最高分数。

## 说明

第二个样例对应的图示如上。红色光束获得了 $10 + 50 + 5 + 35 + 8 + 2 = 110$ 分，而蓝色光束获得了 $120$ 分。

**题面中的图片展示的红色光束只是激光束可能经过的大致路径，这仅用于说明激光束如何获得分数。因此，对于第二个样例，不存在能够获得 110 分的光束。**
</statement>
